statement: Airbus lists the A330-200F in its freighter family separately from the A330-200P2F and A330-300P2F, which it describes as 'Passenger-to-Freighter Airbus supported conversion program'.
notes: Purpose-built (factory) freighter. Not the same aircraft as the converted A330-200P2F.

statement: Boeing describes 'our family of production and converted freighters' and lists the 777 Freighter as the 'Industry standard large widebody freighter'.
notes: Purpose-built (factory) freighter. ICAO designator B77L is shared with the 777-200LR.

statement: Boeing lists the '767-300 Freighter' separately from the '767-300 Boeing Converted Freighter' (767-300BCF).
notes: Purpose-built (factory) freighter. Converted 767-300s (e.g. 767-300BCF) are different aircraft.

statement: Boeing press release 'Boeing Delivers Japan Airlines' First 747-400 Freighter' (12 Oct 2004); a separate 2005 release describes the first 747-400 Boeing Converted Freighter, a passenger jet 'transformed' into a freighter.
notes: Purpose-built (factory) freighter, no longer produced (the final 747, delivered in January 2023, was a 747-8F). Converted 747-400s (BCF, BDSF) are different aircraft.

statement: EFW performs the A321P2F conversion; its STC 'covers all weight variants of A321-200'; Airbus provides 'full OEM data support'.
notes: Passenger-to-freighter conversion of the A321-200 passenger aircraft. This is the only one of the five targets that is an EFW conversion product.
